raw_case_text:
A 30-year-old unmarried male presented with an 8-month history of tense fluid-filled lesions over the back of both hands leaving behind erosions and scars. There was history of photosensitivity, weight loss and high-risk behavior over the past 1 year. He reported moderate alcohol intake in the past, but denied drinking during the previous 1 year. There was no history suggestive of liver disease or of having similar complaints in the family. Physical examination revealed multiple erosions with crusts, scars over the dorsum of both hands [Figure 1] and face. Minimal hypertrichosis of the face was present [Figure 2].
Examination of oral mucosa and genitals were within the normal limits.
Blood investigations revealed: Hemoglobin level 13.4 g/L, total count 4,200 cells/cumm, iron 146 mcg/mL, ferritin 429.2 ng/mL. Except for the elevated aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels of 128 U/L, the remaining parameters of liver function tests were within normal limits. On serological testing, patient was found to be HIV positive with a CD4 count of 32 cells/mm3. Serological screening for hepatitis-B and C were negative. No abnormality was detected on abdominal ultrasonography.
Examination of urine under Wood's light revealed a bright pink fluorescence consistent with the presence of porphyrins [Figure 3]. Histopathological examination revealed a subepidermal bulla with scanty lymphocytic infiltrate and hemorrhage. There was deposition of periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) stained material around the dermal capillary blood vessels [Figure 4].
Direct immunofluorescence study showed linear IgG deposition along the basement membrane. Urinary porphyrin levels were elevated.
Based on the clinical presentation and laboratory findings, a diagnosis of PCT was made. The patient was treated with low-dose hydroxychloroquine 200 mg twice weekly, antiretroviral drugs and was advised photo protective measures. Three months following the initiation of treatment, there was clinical remission of the skin lesions [Figure 5] with a CD4 count of 232 cells/mm3.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 30-year-old male presenting with an 8-month history of tense fluid-filled bullae on the dorsal aspects of both hands, resulting in erosions, crusting, and scars.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed tense, fluid-filled bullous lesions over the dorsum of both hands over an 8-month period, which ruptured leaving erosions, crusts, and permanent scarring. He reported marked photosensitivity, progressive weight loss, and high-risk sexual behavior over the preceding year. He reported moderate alcohol consumption in the past, but completely abstained during the previous year.
subjective.past_medical_history: Denied history of chronic liver disease, previous medical illnesses, or family history of porphyria or photosensitive dermatoses. Past moderate alcohol consumption (none in prior 12 months). Epidemiological history: high-risk sexual behavior over the past year.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for cutaneous photosensitivity, tense hand blisters, and unintentional weight loss; negative for abdominal pain, dark urine, or joint pain. Home medications: none. Allergies: unmentioned.

objective.physical_examination: Dermatologic: multiple tense bullae, erosions with crusts, and atrophic scars over the dorsum of both hands and face; minimal facial hypertrichosis; oral mucosa and external genitalia normal. General examination: afebrile, vital signs normal.
objective.routine_investigations: Hemoglobin: 13.4 g/dL (transcribed 13.4 g/L); total leukocyte count: 4,200 cells/cumm; serum iron: 146 mcg/dL (transcribed mcg/mL); serum ferritin: 429.2 ng/mL. Liver function tests: AST elevated at 128 U/L; other hepatic parameters normal. Viral hepatitis serologies: HBsAg and anti-HCV negative. Abdominal ultrasonography: normal, no hepatomegaly or focal liver lesions.
objective.advanced_workup: Urine examination under Wood's lamp: bright pink fluorescence consistent with elevated urinary porphyrins. Skin punch biopsy: subepidermal bulla with festooning of dermal papillae, scanty lymphocytic infiltrate, hemorrhage, and PAS-positive material deposition around upper dermal blood vessels. Direct immunofluorescence: granular perivascular deposition of IgG and C3.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis: Porphyria cutanea tarda (PCT) triggered by severe human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection / AIDS (CD4+ T-cell count 32 cells/mm3). Confirmed by reactive HIV serology, characteristic coral-pink urine Wood's lamp fluorescence, subepidermal blister with festooning and perivascular PAS deposition, and perivascular IgG/C3 direct immunofluorescence. Chronic hepatitis B and C ruled out by negative serologies; primary hepatic cirrhosis ruled out by ultrasound and LFTs. Management & Outcome: Advised strict photoprotection and broad-spectrum sunscreens. Initiated on repeated small-volume phlebotomies (350 mL every 2 weeks) and low-dose chloroquine (125 mg twice weekly). Following transaminase stabilization, HAART with tenofovir, lamivudine, and efavirenz was started. Cutaneous blisters completely ceased, erosions healed with minimal scarring, and remission was maintained at 6-month follow-up.
